newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX hopes to revive fuel oil futures on Monday.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX hopes to revive fuel oil futures on Monday.

text.p: The Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) hopes to revive its fuel oil futures contract by urging traders to trade the contract from Monday, SIMEX's President Ang Swee Tian said on Friday.

"The trading community have expressed keen interest on the contract and a group of them are trying to make a concerted effort to try to revive and re-activate the contract," Ang told Reuters by telephone.
"They have indicated that from Monday they will try to do something," Ang said.
He said the trading community had proposed changes to the contract earlier this year and they were under consideration.
"At this stage, there has been no decision taken by SIMEX to change the contract yet," he told Reuters.

The proposed changes included lowering the sulphur content to 3.5 percent from 4.0 percent on the fuel oil delivered against the contract and narrowing the loading-date window for physical deliveries.
The contract was launched in February 1989 but trade ground to a halt early last year owing to illiquidity.
Some brokers expressed scepticism that much trade would take place from Monday, especially as the contract;s specifications has not altered since trading ground to a halt.
SIMEX currently operates a mutual offset system with the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) in London to trade the Brent futures contract.
